name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest open PR first. It tests the latest routing paths and prompt versions against real-world inputs, catching edge cases the oldest PR won’t expose. The trade-off is higher risk of noise in newer PRs, but that’s the point—we need to validate against current behavior, not legacy patterns.

name: Gauge
text: PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest open PR risks exposing *new* edge cases that don’t reflect stable behavior—meaning we could waste time debugging transient issues instead of validating against proven routing. Better to run it on the oldest merged PR first: it tests against a known-good state, and any failures there are real regressions, not noise. Settle it by comparing the two runs—if the oldest PR’s shadow mode catches more actionable issues, it wins.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest open PR *and* the oldest merged PR simultaneously to compare outputs directly—this cuts time by eliminating sequential waits while still covering both stable and edge-case routing paths. The extra noise from newer PRs becomes manageable by filtering for only the most impactful differences between the two runs.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the oldest merged PR first. It tests against a stable baseline, so any noise from edge cases in newer PRs doesn’t pollute validation of proven routing paths. The trade-off is missing fresh edge cases, but those can be caught later—first we lock in correctness on known-good behavior.
